title: CJP Sacks Spokesperson Vijeta Dahiya After Viral Burger Video Sparks Backlash
excerpt: The Cockroach Janta Party removed Dahiya from all official duties after he dismissed accountability to protesters, calling their criticism "nonsense."
body:
Key Takeaways
  • CJP dismissed spokesperson Vijeta Dahiya after a viral video showed him dismissing a protester.
  • Dahiya's remarks were deemed 'deeply insensitive' by CJP leadership.
  • The incident occurred during CJP's 'Chalo Sansad' march, which drew tens of thousands.
  • CJP's credibility relies on grassroots participation and member accountability.
  • The movement has gained significant support from the Indian diaspora globally.
CJP's Response to Dahiya's Controversy
›Dahiya removed from all official duties.
›CJP condemned his actions as inconsistent with movement values.
›Dahiya was one of three spokespersons appointed in June.
›CJP emerged from a satirical movement in late 2025.
Source: News Article
> **""We strongly condemn the deeply insensitive actions of Vijeta Dahiya."**

The Cockroach Janta Party removed Vijeta Dahiya as its spokesperson on Tuesday and relieved him of all official duties, after a viral video showed a protester confronting Dahiya for eating a burger at a restaurant while fellow CJP supporters demonstrated nearby.

In the video, the protester asked Dahiya why he was eating out instead of participating in the CJP-led agitation. Dahiya responded dismissively.

"You hold me accountable as if it is my job to be a protester. Have you elected me? This is nonsense."

— Vijeta Dahiya, Former CJP Spokesperson

CJP Moves Swiftly to Distance Itself

CJP issued a statement condemning Dahiya's remarks in strong terms. "We strongly condemn the deeply insensitive actions of Vijeta Dahiya. His conduct is wholly inconsistent with the values and ethos of this movement," the party said.

Dahiya, a political researcher, author and filmmaker, had been appointed as one of three CJP spokespersons in June, alongside investigative journalist Saurav Das and IIT Kanpur alumnus Ashutosh Ranka. Das remains the party's chief spokesperson.

The incident is particularly damaging because it cuts at the heart of CJP's identity as a grassroots movement driven by ordinary citizens who feel betrayed by the political establishment. The party, which emerged from a satirical social media movement in late 2025, has built its credibility on the participation and sacrifice of its supporters, many of whom are students and young professionals.

A Movement Under Strain

The removal comes at a turbulent moment for the Cockroach movement. On Monday, CJP's 'Chalo Sansad' march drew tens of thousands of protesters to the area around Parliament as India's monsoon session opened. Videos circulating on social media appeared to show police using batons to disperse demonstrators advancing from Jantar Mantar toward Parliament, though Delhi Police denied any use of force.

Leader of the Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge raised the issue in the Rajya Sabha, alleging that students had been subjected to a lathi charge. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray called the reported use of force "cowardly," while NCP (SCP) MP Supriya Sule described it as "deeply unfortunate and unacceptable."

Meanwhile, activist Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike in support of the movement has entered its 23rd day, with the Delhi High Court recently allowing his transfer to Medanta Hospital.

Why It Matters for the Diaspora

CJP's protest movement has resonated strongly with Indians abroad, who have staged solidarity demonstrations outside Indian diplomatic missions in London, Washington and other cities. The party's core demand — the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak scandal — has become a rallying point for diaspora communities frustrated with examination irregularities.

The Dahiya episode is a test of the movement's internal discipline. By acting swiftly to remove him, CJP's leadership appears to be signaling that the movement's credibility depends on its members living the values they preach — including solidarity with those on the streets.
